paras: Robots need a hand that can pick, move, and grip objects easily to help them work in real life. Building such a hand is very hard because it must be strong, flexible, and simple to make. Boston Dynamics says their new robot hand should have three fingers and one thumb.

news.title: Glowing 'cauldron' of new stars | Space photo of the day for Oct. 26, 2026
paras: The James Webb Space Telescope captured a spectacular star-forming region glowing 161,000 light-years from Earth in a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way. The NASA/ESA James Webb Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of a majestic star-forming region shining 161,000 light-years from Earth in a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way known as the Large Magellanic Cloud.

The deep-space image reveals a 230-light-year-wide swathe of the glowing emission nebula N159, threaded with denser filaments of reddish molecular hydrogen that hide countless energetic young stars . Ghostly blue clouds of ionized hydrogen gas (H II) glow in the center of the image, having been energized by the ultraviolet radiation pouring out from nearby stars, whose winds helped create the chaotic structure of the vast stellar nursery.

news.title: 'More missions, more often': NASA is overhauling how it selects science missions
paras: The new approach, called Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), was announced on Oct. 21 in an open letter from Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate (SMD), to the NASA science community.

The changes, directed by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, could significantly reshape how scientists, universities, NASA centers and commercial companies vie for future missions. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long," Fox stated in the letter. The new process aims to prioritize scientific merit over unduly complicated engineering and financial planning during initial evaluations, and reduce selection timelines to encourage innovation.

news.title: On this day in space! Oct. 25, 1671: Astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovers Iapetus, Saturn's 'yin-yang' moon
paras: 25, 1671, the Italian astronomer Giovanni Cassini discovered a new moon at Saturn! Iapetus was the second moon anyone had ever found orbiting Saturn, and it was the first of four moons Cassini would discover at the ringed planet. The Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens had discovered Titan , the largest of Saturn's moons, about six years earlier.

After Cassini found Iapetus, he also found the moons Rhea, Tethys and Dione. When Cassini first saw Iapetus, the moon looked like a tiny speck on the west side of Saturn. He calculated its orbit and thought he would be able to see it again on the east side of Saturn 39 days later, but it was nowhere to be seen.

sport.title: What the ITIA’s New Anti-Doping Rules Mean for Players Going Into 2027
paras: The changes, announced on Wednesday, October 21, will require players in the Registered Testing Pool (RTP) to provide a daily 60-minute window during which they can be tested, including while competing at tournaments. Tennis previously received an exemption because of the unpredictable nature of players’ schedules.

However, the ITIA will reduce the size of its RTP, transferring around 80% of its current members to an expanded testing pool where the daily 60-minute window will not be required. Players remaining in the reduced RTP must provide the designated time slot both in and out of competition.
